cards.title: Competitor offer and profitability scan
cards.claim: Competitor analysis can capture the promise, target-person clarity, deliverables, price, mass-market positioning, and professional presentation; competitors making serious money can signal a profitable market and idea.
cards.action: When analyzing a market, identify the competitor's promise, what they are offering (e.g., program format, videos, nutrition plan, bonuses), price, whether it is mass-market, and whether the presentation looks professional; treat evidence that competitors are making serious money as a positive market signal.
applies_when: evaluating an existing market with competitor offers
competitor promise, deliverables, price, mass-market positioning, and professional presentation can be observed
there is evidence competitors are making serious money
do_not_use_when: you have no evidence competitors are making serious money
you treat competitor profitability as proof your exact offer will succeed
you cannot observe competitor offer details
unknowns: whether competitor profitability comes from factors you can replicate
evidence_quotes: here's the promise 25 minutes is all it takes to get ripped to get abs lose the baby fat get the six-pack feel better look better fast
notice that there's nothing here about the specific type of person it's for
what are they offering it's a 14 week DVD program get a bunch of videos of the workouts a nutrition plan plus a handful of bonuses
it's only 60 dollars total
this is a mass-market product
look professional
there is a serious business behind this these people are making serious money that's a good sign
you want your competitors to be making money because if they weren't it wouldn't be a profitable market and a profitable idea for you

cards.title: Review and forum mining
cards.claim: Amazon top-book reviews, including two-to-four-star reviews, plus Reddit/Quora discussions can reveal likes, criticisms, goals, and pain points; online answers may be unreliable.
cards.action: Search Amazon for the top five to ten books in the market; read reviews for what people liked and read two-to-four-star reviews for criticisms; search Reddit/Quora with specific niche queries to find goals and pain points; beware lies and answers people think others want to hear, but still listen for nuggets of truth.
applies_when: doing market research for a niche product
using Amazon top books/reviews, Reddit, or Quora
seeking pain points, desired outcomes, and criticisms
do_not_use_when: you assume all online answers are truthful
you rely on a single review or comment
you cannot distinguish legitimate criticism from keyboard warriors
unknowns: how many sources or reviews are enough
how to distinguish legitimate criticism from keyboard warriors
evidence_quotes: let's go on to Amazon to find the top five to ten books in the market
look through the reviews for what people really liked about it
let's also look at the two to four star reviews to see what criticisms there were
you will get more sensitive to being able to tell legitimately giving you criticism and who's just a keyboard warrior
this is where you're really gonna start finding nuggets about people's goals and pain points
now just beware you're gonna find a lot of answers you're also gonna find a lot of lies a lot of lies when it comes to people answering stuff online
people give answers that they think other people want to hear
you still want to listen and really find out those nuggets of truth

cards.title: Prior-spend, no-result best customers
cards.claim: Best customers can be people who already spent time or money trying to solve the problem but have not gotten the results they want.
cards.action: When a review, comment, or customer research call shows prior time/money spend without desired results, lean in and ask 'tell me more'; treat that person as a potential best customer.
applies_when: a review, comment, or customer call shows prior time or money spent on the problem
the person has not gotten desired results and still has the problem
they are self-aware and serious about solving it
do_not_use_when: the person is a keyboard warrior who reads about diets/workouts but does not go to the gym or change diet
there is no evidence of prior time/money spend or unresolved result
unknowns: whether that person will buy from you
evidence_quotes: I spent thousands of dollars to hire personal trainers to go through a variety of exercises however never get quite satisfied
your best best customers are going to be people who have already spent time or money solving the problem that you're solving but they haven't gotten the results they want
if they have spent time and/or money that means they recognize there's a problem
they haven't gotten the results they want
